ProjectList.title: Frontend Portfolio
ProjectList.description: This project was my very first capstone at the Zuitt Coding Bootcamp. It serves as both a portfolio and a milestone in my journey as a developer. Built with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Bootstrap, this project allowed me to focus on clean, responsive design principles while showcasing my earliest works. It helped me understand the importance of structuring content for both usability and visual appeal, laying the foundation for the rest of my projects.

ProjectList.title: Backend API
ProjectList.description: As the second capstone project, this REST API was built to power an e-commerce application. It was developed using Node.js and Express, with full CRUD functionality, user authentication, and secure routing. This project pushed me deeper into backend development and helped me understand how APIs serve as the backbone of scalable applications. It was also my first real experience in connecting frontend applications with server-side logic.

ProjectList.title: Full-Stack React App
ProjectList.description: This was my final capstone project at Zuitt — a full-stack e-commerce application built using React for the frontend and a REST API backend. The app includes features such as product browsing, user authentication, shopping cart management, and order processing. This project represented a culmination of everything I learned during the bootcamp and gave me hands-on experience in managing state, API integration, and building user-friendly interfaces at scale.

ProjectList.title: Simple Calculator
ProjectList.description: A straightforward but practical project that helped me reinforce JavaScript fundamentals. The calculator supports basic mathematical operations and includes a history feature to track past calculations. Beyond its simplicity, this project challenged me to think about DOM manipulation, event handling, and maintaining a clean user interface. I also implemented small quality-of-life improvements, like real-time operation updates, to make it more user-friendly.

ProjectList.title: Animated Login Form
ProjectList.description: This project focused entirely on UI and animation, allowing me to explore CSS transitions and keyframe animations. The login form is designed with smooth animations for inputs and labels, giving the interface a polished, modern feel. While the form’s backend functionality is not implemented, this project was more about experimenting with micro-interactions and learning how subtle animations can dramatically improve user experience.

ProjectList.title: Personal Blog
ProjectList.description: This project is a personal blog application that I update as part of my growth as a developer. Built as a full-stack app, it allows me to write, edit, and share articles. The project combines frontend design with backend API integration, providing a complete content management experience. Through building this, I gained deeper insight into routing, data persistence, and deployment processes for production-ready apps.

ProjectList.title: Blog API
ProjectList.description: This is the backend API that powers my personal blog. Built with Node.js and Express, it supports essential features such as creating, editing, and deleting posts, along with user authentication and session management. Working on this project allowed me to deepen my understanding of RESTful API design and gave me experience in structuring code for maintainability and scalability.

ProjectList.title: Weather App
ProjectList.description: This weather app was created using React and consumes the WeatherAPI service to provide real-time weather updates. The app allows users to search for cities and view forecasts. Beyond fetching and displaying data, this project helped me practice API integration, error handling, and conditional rendering, as well as refining responsive design for a clean and accessible user experience.

ProjectList.title: To-do List
ProjectList.description: A classic to-do list app built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, this project includes features such as adding tasks, marking them as complete, deleting items, and rearranging the task order. I also experimented with making it a Chrome extension, which taught me how browser APIs interact with simple web apps. It was a great exercise in building practical tools while solidifying DOM manipulation skills.

ProjectList.title: BMI Calculator
ProjectList.description: A lightweight, static web application for calculating and tracking Body Mass Index (BMI) with a modern dark theme. Features a step-by-step wizard interface with flexible unit selection (independent units for weight and height, including feet & inches format), in-depth health analysis based on age and sex factors, comprehensive history tracking with clickable entries, and full unit conversion display. The app runs entirely client-side using localStorage for data persistence, includes accessibility features (ARIA labels, keyboard navigation), and provides clear data storage warnings. Built with vanilla JavaScript and Alpine.js for reactive UI, styled with Tailwind CSS using a carefully designed dark color scheme that's easy on the eyes.

ProjectList.title: ReUseMe
ProjectList.description: A lightweight, web application for creating a quick harvard style resume. Has User Profiles and versions tailored for different companies. Only deployed locally, with an sqlite database for fast deployment

ProjectList.title: Job Application Tracker
ProjectList.description: A laravel app used to track job appplication on different job sites. supports multiple person. only deployed locally.

ProjectList.title: Weddsite
ProjectList.description: A static website that offers wedding web services.

ProjectList.title: Cover Letter Generator
ProjectList.description: An attempt of vibe coding to deploy locally a cover letter generator based on uploaded resume and pasted job description. uses multi stage AI models to generate a cover letter.
